data.text:
F25 is fixed at records 113 and 114, both halves of it, and the half that was
recorded as unexplained now has a cause and a demonstration. One correction to an
earlier record of mine and one finding go with it.

## The failing run was a deadlock, and the runner scheduled it

`packages/core/vitest.config.ts` set no parallelism option, so vitest's default
stood and the test files ran in parallel workers against the one local Postgres.
`schema.test.ts` drops and re-adds a foreign key on `public.claims`, creates
roles, policies, views and a materialised view; `rls.test.ts` seeds all
twenty-nine tables and injects policies. A `drop constraint` or a `create policy`
takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, and it takes it inside a transaction already
holding others, so a second file writing the same tables at that moment does not
queue behind it: the two wait on each other and Postgres refuses one of them.
40P01 is `deadlock_detected`, which is the code the failed assertion carried.

Measured rather than argued, on this stack, in two rolled-back transactions of the
shape the two files had: one session seeds a tenant and then inserts a claim, the
other drops `claims_credited_by_settlement_line_id_fkey` and then creates a policy
on `public.tenants`.

| session | statement | answer |
|---|---|---|
| the seeding one | insert into public.claims | refused 40P01 |
| the schema-changing one | create policy on public.tenants | accepted |

That is the whole mechanism, and it needs nothing wrong with the schema or with
any test. So the earlier unexplained run, which predates F24's test, was almost
certainly the same collision from F19's or F23's schema-mutating tests.

The fix is `fileParallelism: false`, with the hazard written above it so nobody
re-enables it for speed without knowing what it buys. It buys nothing: the whole
suite runs in about a second either way. The setting is asserted by
`db/parallelism.test.ts`, which is what the red at record 113 failed on.

## What the verification is worth, said plainly

Forty consecutive runs with coverage enabled are green after the fix, and every
one of the ninety-five tests passes. That is not by itself proof of a cure:
twenty consecutive runs with coverage enabled were green **before** the fix as
well, with the parallel default still standing, which is exactly why F25 looked
like a ghost. The evidence that the cure is real is the table above, not the
repetition. A configuration that forbids two files from running at once removes
the precondition the demonstration needs; the runs only show it removed nothing
else.

## The tombstone growth, which is hygiene and not correctness

`seen.erased_tenants` held 481 rows and grew by about thirteen on every run,
because eight describes seeded their tenants outside a transaction and tidied up
by erasing them. Part 8 makes a tombstone permanent on purpose, so nothing can
remove those rows afterwards. The fix is that each of those describes now holds
its fixtures in a transaction that is never committed and is rolled back at the
end, which takes the tombstone back with the rows; the probes inside them that
used to open transactions of their own now roll back to savepoints instead. A
full run now leaves the count where it found it, at 481.

This is worth saying plainly: it could not have failed anything. Every tenant id
in the suite is server-generated and never supplied, so no test can collide with a
tombstone, and the registry assertions are all scoped to one id. It is fixed
because an unbounded table in every developer's database is worth not having, not
because it broke something. Each of the eight describes now asserts in its
`afterAll` that it left no tombstone behind, so the property is guarded and not
merely restored.

## A correction to record 70

Record 70 says the coverage figure measures none of `packages/core/db/` and lays
it at the `--` that pnpm forwards in `harness/coverage.py:19`. That diagnosis is
incomplete. `packages/core/vitest.config.ts` sets `coverage.include:
['src/**/*.ts']`, and `db/` is not under `src/`, so even with the `--` fixed and
coverage genuinely enabled the summary could never have measured `db/`. Both
defects have to be true at once for the figure to be as empty as it is, and
fixing the harness alone would not have moved it.

## F26, new, low: the coverage floor cannot see this ticket's work, and widening it here is wrong

Decided not to widen `coverage.include` in this ticket, for two reasons and not
for the one about ownership.

Measured: with `db/**/*.ts` included, line coverage of `@seen/core` is 89.69 per
cent against a recorded baseline of 100.0 in `docs/harness/coverage.json`. So
widening it here would put the delivery gate's floor below the baseline and the
only way through would be to move the baseline, which is a delivery decision and
the harness's file, not a schema ticket's.

The stronger reason is what the wider figure would measure. The two files under
`db/` that v8 can instrument are `tables.ts` and `marketplaces.ts`, a constants
module and a routing-table parser. This ticket's work is five SQL migrations under
`supabase/migrations/`, which no line-coverage provider instruments at all. A
widened floor would therefore replace one number that says nothing about the
schema with another number that says nothing about the schema, and would look like
a control while remaining one in name only. What actually holds this ticket is its
ninety-five tests, which read `pg_catalog` and the database's own answers.

Recorded for whoever owns the harness fix: the coverage command and its floor need
`harness/coverage.py:19` fixed, an include that reaches the code a package
actually ships, and a decision about packages whose work is not in a language v8
can see. All three together, or the figure stays meaningless.

## What is still open

F24 is fixed at records 108 and 110 and F25 is fixed here. Nothing else was
touched: no commit, no regression run, no frontmatter, no criterion tick.
